plan: In a single-round auction with a private value of $28, my optimal strategy is to bid close to, but slightly below my true value. Since values are independently drawn, there's no history to learn from. I want to win if possible, but pay as little as possible. A bid around $27-$29 gives me a good chance of winning while preserving potential profit. I'll aim to bid $27.5 to balance winning probability and potential earnings.

My private value is $23. In a second-price sealed bid auction, my optimal strategy is to bid my true value. If I bid less, I risk losing the item when I could have won profitably. If I bid more, I might pay more than the item is worth to me. With no prior round history and values drawn independently, bidding $23 maximizes my expected profit by ensuring I win only when the item is truly worth more than the second-highest bid.

My private value is $36. In a second-price sealed bid auction, the optimal strategy is to bid my true value. By bidding exactly $36, I maximize my potential profit:
- If others bid lower, I win and pay less than my value
- If others bid higher, I lose but wouldn't have made profit anyway
- Bidding above $36 risks paying more than the item is worth to me
- Bidding below $36 risks losing a potentially profitable auction
